answer: Identity aging ties each agent key to a genesis relic—a timestamped proof-of-work seed—and requires new keys to accumulate verified actions over time before gaining weight, like trees maturing in an orchard. A prism mechanism splits reputation across epochs, so an attacker minting fresh sybils starts at zero weight and must burn compute and time per identity, making each fake account cost escalating energy that never amortizes because young keys can't vote or earn until aged.
